observation: After Gemini’s first response, the user wanted the exact answer rather than a formula. The user cared about the result, not the process.

In the second prompt, the user asked “Can you directly access my photo file and just tell me…”. The phrasing of the prompt as a question might suggest that the user is unsure of the AI's ability to read the provided data. When Gemini delivered, that confirmed or built a mental model of the tool as able to operate on their data.

The user defined summer as “June to September” rather than leaving it for Gemini to figure out. In my runs, Gemini defaulted to June–August, which produced a different correct answer. The user resolved the ambiguity themselves, without realizing the model had a different default.

The user checked the spreadsheet manually after getting the answer. Even a confident, correct answer didn’t earn full trust right away. The user still treated AI output as something to check, especially for a concrete, checkable fact.
